audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Numbers / Bemidbar red-cow and corpse-impurity purification text tradition, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for red-cow rite, outside-camp burning, cedar/hyssop/scarlet, ash collection, corpse impurity, tent and grave contact, third/seventh-day sprinkling, and paradoxical impurity of ritual handlers. Anti-stigma and medical-safety safeguards required.

verses.restored: YHWH spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,

familiar.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying,

verses.restored: This is statute of Torah/instruction that YHWH commanded, saying: Speak to children of Israel, and let them take to you a red cow, complete, in which there is no defect, upon which no yoke has gone up.

familiar.text: This is the ordinance of the law which the LORD hath commanded, saying, Speak unto the children of Israel, that they bring thee a red heifer without spot, wherein is no blemish, and upon which never came yoke:

verses.restored: You shall give her to Eleazar the priest, and he shall bring her outside camp, and she shall be slaughtered before him.

familiar.text: And ye shall give her unto Eleazar the priest, that he may bring her forth without the camp, and one shall slay her before his face:

verses.restored: Eleazar the priest shall take from her blood with his finger and sprinkle toward face/front of tent of meeting from her blood seven times.

familiar.text: And Eleazar the priest shall take of her blood with his finger, and sprinkle of her blood directly before the tabernacle of the congregation seven times:

verses.restored: The cow shall be burned before his eyes; her hide, flesh, blood, and dung shall be burned.

familiar.text: And one shall burn the heifer in his sight; her skin, and her flesh, and her blood, with her dung, shall he burn:

verses.restored: The priest shall take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet material and cast them into midst of burning cow.

familiar.text: And the priest shall take cedar wood, and hyssop, and scarlet, and cast it into the midst of the burning of the heifer.

verses.restored: The priest shall wash his garments and bathe his flesh in water; afterward he may enter camp, but priest shall be unclean until evening.

familiar.text: Then the priest shall wash his clothes, and he shall bathe his flesh in water, and afterward he shall come into the camp, and the priest shall be unclean until the even.

verses.restored: The one burning her shall wash his garments in water and bathe his flesh in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.

familiar.text: And he that burneth her shall wash his clothes in water, and bathe his flesh in water, and shall be unclean until the even.

verses.restored: A clean man shall gather ashes of cow and deposit them outside camp in clean place; they shall be kept for congregation of children of Israel for water of impurity-removal; it is a sin/purification offering.

familiar.text: And a man that is clean shall gather up the ashes of the heifer, and lay them up without the camp in a clean place, and it shall be kept for the congregation of the children of Israel for a water of separation: it is a purification for sin.

verses.restored: The one gathering ashes of cow shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening. It shall be for children of Israel and for sojourner sojourning in their midst as age-long statute.

familiar.text: And he that gathereth the ashes of the heifer shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the even: and it shall be unto the children of Israel, and unto the stranger that sojourneth among them, for a statute for ever.

verses.restored: The one touching dead body of any human soul/life shall be unclean seven days.

familiar.text: He that toucheth the dead body of any man shall be unclean seven days.

verses.restored: He shall purify himself with it on third day and on seventh day he shall be clean; but if he does not purify himself on third day and seventh day, he shall not be clean.

familiar.text: He shall purify himself with it on the third day, and on the seventh day he shall be clean: but if he purify not himself the third day, then the seventh day he shall not be clean.

verses.restored: Everyone touching dead body, soul/life of a human who died, and not purifying himself, makes dwelling-place of YHWH unclean; that soul/life shall be cut off from Israel. Because water of impurity-removal was not sprinkled upon him, unclean he shall be; his uncleanness remains upon him.

familiar.text: Whosoever toucheth the dead body of any man that is dead, and purifieth not himself, defileth the tabernacle of the LORD; and that soul shall be cut off from Israel: because the water of separation was not sprinkled upon him, he shall be unclean; his uncleanness is yet upon him.

verses.restored: This is Torah/instruction when a human dies in a tent: everyone entering tent and everyone in tent shall be unclean seven days.

familiar.text: This is the law, when a man dieth in a tent: all that come into the tent, and all that is in the tent, shall be unclean seven days.

verses.restored: Every open vessel upon which no covering is fastened shall be unclean.

familiar.text: And every open vessel, which hath no covering bound upon it, is unclean.

verses.restored: Everyone who in open field touches one slain by sword, or a dead body, or human bone, or grave shall be unclean seven days.

familiar.text: And whosoever toucheth one that is slain with a sword in the open fields, or a dead body, or a bone of a man, or a grave, shall be unclean seven days.

verses.restored: For the unclean they shall take from ashes of burning of sin/purification offering and put living/running water upon them in a vessel.

familiar.text: And for an unclean person they shall take of the ashes of the burnt heifer of purification for sin, and running water shall be put thereto in a vessel:

verses.restored: A clean man shall take hyssop and dip it in water and sprinkle upon tent, all vessels, and persons who were there, and upon one who touched bone, slain one, dead one, or grave.

familiar.text: And a clean person shall take hyssop, and dip it in the water, and sprinkle it upon the tent, and upon all the vessels, and upon the persons that were there, and upon him that touched a bone, or one slain, or one dead, or a grave:

verses.restored: The clean shall sprinkle upon unclean on third day and seventh day; on seventh day he shall purify him. He shall wash his garments and bathe in water, and at evening he shall be clean.

familiar.text: And the clean person shall sprinkle upon the unclean on the third day, and on the seventh day: and on the seventh day he shall purify himself, and wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and shall be clean at even.

verses.restored: But a man who becomes unclean and does not purify himself, that soul/life shall be cut off from midst of assembly, because sanctuary of YHWH he made unclean; water of impurity-removal was not sprinkled upon him; unclean he is.

familiar.text: But the man that shall be unclean, and shall not purify himself, that soul shall be cut off from among the congregation, because he hath defiled the sanctuary of the LORD: the water of separation hath not been sprinkled upon him; he is unclean.

verses.restored: It shall be for them as age-long statute: one sprinkling water of impurity-removal shall wash his garments, and one touching water of impurity-removal shall be unclean until evening.

familiar.text: And it shall be a perpetual statute unto them, that he that sprinkleth the water of separation shall wash his clothes; and he that toucheth the water of separation shall be unclean until even.

verses.restored: Whatever unclean one touches shall be unclean, and soul/life touching it shall be unclean until evening.

familiar.text: And whatsoever the unclean person toucheth shall be unclean; and the soul that toucheth it shall be unclean until even.

translation_notes: Corpse impurity is a ritual condition associated with death, not moral guilt, sinfulness of grief, or reduced human worth.
The red-cow rite occurs outside camp and produces ashes mixed with living water for later sprinkling.
Those who prepare or handle the purifying materials become temporarily unclean, creating a deliberate ritual paradox: the agent of purification also bears impurity.
The same statute applies to Israelite and sojourner.
The rite is not modern sanitation, medicine, disinfectant, or evidence-based treatment and must not replace healthcare.
Cut-off language is severe ancient sanctuary-boundary material and must not authorize punishment of mourners or those handling the dead.
safety_note: Do not use Numbers 19 to stigmatize grief, death-care workers, illness, disability, menstruation, or bodies; do not reproduce the animal rite or substitute ritual water for medical care. The chapter regulates ancient sanctuary access after contact with death.
